hot.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
hot.summary: Meta-Harness provides an end-to-end optimization framework for LLM harnesses, the external code that dictates how models interact with their environment. The system utilizes an agentic proposer with filesystem access to uncompressed historical code and execution traces, leading to a 7.7-point accuracy improvement in text classification, a 4.7-point average gain in math reasoning, and competitive pass rates on agentic coding benchmarks.

hot.title: Screening Is Enough
hot.summary: Microsoft developed the AI Greenferencing framework and its Heron router, enabling the routing of AI inferencing workloads to modular data centers located at wind farms. This system leverages underutilized renewable energy and helps mitigate strain on the power grid, demonstrating a 1.8x goodput improvement and a 27% median end-to-end latency reduction for AI tasks through intelligent routing and multi-timescale resource optimization.

hot.title: Think Anywhere in Code Generation
hot.summary: Peking University and Alibaba Group researchers developed THINK-ANYWHERE, a mechanism enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to invoke on-demand, token-level reasoning during code generation, enhancing adaptability and resource efficiency. The approach achieves an average pass@1 score of 70.3% across four code generation benchmarks, representing a 9.3% absolute improvement, and also generalizes to mathematical reasoning tasks.

hot.title: SKILL0: In-Context Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Skill Internalization
hot.summary: The SKILL0 framework introduces In-Context Reinforcement Learning (ICRL) to enable Large Language Model (LLM) agents to internalize skills into their parameters, thereby achieving autonomous behavior without external skill descriptions at inference time. This approach yielded superior performance, such as an 87.9% success rate on ALFWorld (+9.7% over AgentOCR), while substantially reducing context token costs by over 5 times compared to skill-augmented methods.

hot.title: The Latent Space: Foundation, Evolution, Mechanism, Ability, and Outlook
hot.summary: A comprehensive survey unifies the fragmented understanding of latent space in language-based models, detailing its conceptual foundation, historical evolution, technical mechanisms, emergent abilities, and future research directions. It positions latent space as a machine-native computational substrate enabling enhanced intelligence beyond explicit token-level operations.

hot.title: Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation
hot.summary: A method called Simple Self-Distillation (SSD) enables large language models to enhance their code generation performance by training exclusively on self-generated, unverified solutions. This approach improved the Qwen3-30B-Instruct model's pass@1 score on LiveCodeBench v6 from 42.4% to 55.3%, demonstrating its efficacy without external supervision or complex verification.

hot.title: Understanding Transformers and Attention Mechanisms: An Introduction for Applied Mathematicians
hot.summary: Michel Fabrice Serret's preprint introduces the fundamental concepts of Transformer models and attention mechanisms, tailored for applied mathematicians. It systematically formalizes text encoding, attention operations, architectural components, and discusses computational optimizations like KV caching and latent attention, preparing the audience to engage with quantitative challenges in the field.

hot.title: Generative World Renderer
hot.summary: This research introduces a large-scale dataset, "Generative World Renderer," comprising over 4 million frames from AAA games with synchronized RGB and five G-buffer channels, alongside a novel VLM-based evaluation protocol. The work demonstrates that training on this dataset substantially improves inverse rendering performance and G-buffer-conditioned forward synthesis, enabling more robust material decomposition, precise geometry, and enhanced real-world game editing with complex atmospheric effects.

hot.title: LatentUM: Unleashing the Potential of Interleaved Cross-Modal Reasoning via a Latent-Space Unified Model
hot.summary: Researchers at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, and UCSD developed LatentUM, a unified model that integrates visual understanding and generation within a shared semantic latent space, eliminating pixel-space mediation. This approach enhances interleaved cross-modal reasoning for tasks like visual spatial planning and action-conditioned world modeling, achieving state-of-the-art performance on relevant benchmarks.

hot.title: OmniVoice: Towards Omnilingual Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech with Diffusion Language Models
hot.summary: OmniVoice, developed by Xiaomi Corp., introduces a single-stage, discrete non-autoregressive text-to-speech model supporting over 600 languages with zero-shot capabilities. It achieved competitive intelligibility and speaker similarity across English, Chinese, and diverse multilingual benchmarks, outperforming several commercial systems.

hot.title: UniDriveVLA: Unifying Understanding, Perception, and Action Planning for Autonomous Driving
hot.summary: UniDriveVLA presents a unified Vision-Language-Action model that integrates understanding, perception, and planning for autonomous driving, effectively mitigating the trade-off between spatial awareness and semantic reasoning through a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. The model achieves competitive performance in closed-loop driving (Bench2Drive Driving Score 78.37) and demonstrates high trajectory accuracy on nuScenes, all while preserving general multimodal reasoning abilities.

hot.title: Do Papers with Titles Ending in a Question Mark Usually Have the Answer "No"?
hot.summary: Researchers at The Institute for Interrogative Astrophysics quantitatively examined scientific paper titles ending in a question mark, finding that 40% of such titles amenable to a binary answer resulted in a "no" response, compared to 26% yielding a "yes" answer. The study provides data supporting the applicability of Betteridge's Law within academic publishing.

hot.title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
hot.summary: Chongjie Ye et al. introduce Omni123, a 3D native foundation model that unifies text-to-2D and text-to-3D generation within a single autoregressive framework, leveraging abundant 2D data as a geometric prior to address 3D data scarcity. The model outperforms existing methods in text-to-3D shape generation, achieving superior semantic alignment, and demonstrates enhanced instruction-based 3D editing with lower Chamfer Distance.

hot.title: A Simple Baseline for Streaming Video Understanding
hot.summary: SIMPLESTREAM, a minimalist baseline employing only the most recent N video frames with an off-the-shelf visual-language model, achieves state-of-the-art performance on streaming video understanding benchmarks like OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, demonstrating that complex memory mechanisms are often not necessary for competitive results.

hot.title: Proactive Agent Research Environment: Simulating Active Users to Evaluate Proactive Assistants
hot.summary: The Proactive Agent Research Environment (Pare) and its benchmark Pare-Bench are introduced to simulate active users in stateful mobile environments, providing a realistic platform for evaluating proactive AI assistants. Experiments with frontier LLMs indicated a current task success rate of approximately 42%, revealing challenges in complex proactive scenarios.

hot.title: A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Models
hot.summary: A comprehensive survey outlines On-Policy Distillation (OPD) for Large Language Models (LLMs), introducing a unified theoretical framework based on f-divergences and a three-dimensional taxonomy for existing methods. The work details how OPD mitigates exposure bias, reducing error accumulation from quadratic to linear, and explores various methodologies and future research directions for efficient and capable LLM distillation.

hot.title: Reinforcement Learning for Speculative Trading under Exploratory Framework
hot.summary: This research introduces a reinforcement learning framework for sequential optimal stopping in speculative trading, where agents learn optimal entry and exit times under general price dynamics and utility functions. The methodology employs randomized intensity controls with entropy regularization, yielding closed-form optimal policies as Gibbs distributions and providing theoretical convergence guarantees to the original problem.

hot.title: DVGT-2: Vision-Geometry-Action Model for Autonomous Driving at Scale
hot.summary: Researchers introduce DVGT-2, a Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model that enables real-time, end-to-end autonomous driving by processing dense 3D pointmaps and ego-poses from multi-frame image inputs to predict future trajectories. This streaming architecture achieves constant computational overhead and memory usage, making high-fidelity 3D geometry reconstruction viable for continuous online operation, and establishes new state-of-the-art performance in closed-loop planning on NAVSIM benchmarks while maintaining lower collision rates in open-loop tests.

hot.title: UniMixer: A Unified Architecture for Scaling Laws in Recommendation Systems
hot.summary: Researchers at Kuaishou Technology developed UniMixer, a unified architecture for recommendation systems that bridges attention, TokenMixer, and Factorization Machine paradigms through a parameterized mixing module. The lightweight UniMixer-Lite variant achieved superior scaling efficiency and higher offline AUC (e.g., 0.752327 with 38.2M parameters) compared to prior methods, leading to an average increase of over 15% in user engagement (Cumulative Active Days) in Kuaishou's online advertising scenarios.

hot.title: ASI-Evolve: AI Accelerates AI
hot.summary: ASI-EVOLVE, an agentic framework developed by researchers from SJTU, SII, and GAIR, enables AI to autonomously accelerate its own development by iteratively generating, experimenting with, and analyzing new ideas across model architectures, pretraining data, and reinforcement learning algorithms. The system achieved a +0.97 point gain over human-designed baselines in architecture design, a +3.96 point improvement on AI-curated pretraining data, and up to +12.5 points on mathematical reasoning benchmarks for evolved RL algorithms.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile  Edge Computing
likes.summary: A multi-tier task offloading mechanism for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing efficiently processes sequential subtasks from vehicular applications by first leveraging proximate vehicle resources and then RSU-based MEC. The system minimizes energy consumption while meeting stringent delay requirements through joint optimization of offloading decisions, communication, and computation resource allocation, demonstrating superior performance over various baselines.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
